message.content: Hey, I'm your AI tutor. Today's topic is average speed and rates. You ready to start?
hi yeah im ready let's do this
Hey, awesome, let's get rolling. Picture a driver heading from Delhi to Agra at 30 mph and then back the same way at 60 mph. How would you go about figuring out the average speed for the whole trip?
u just add them and halve it so its 45 mph
Alright, so you're thinking just average the speeds to 45. But if the road from Delhi to Agra is the same distance both ways, how much time does the driver spend going at 30 mph compared to 60 mph?
idk u didnt say how many miles it is so i cant say
Yeah, fair point, no exact miles given. What if you just pick any distance you want for that Delhi to Agra road, like 120 miles one way, and work out the total time for going there and back?
4 hrs there and 2 hrs back so 6 hrs total
Okay, so that's 4 hours going and 2 coming back for 6 hours total. With 240 miles for the whole round trip, how would you figure out the average speed?
do i divide the 6 hours by 2 cos its two legs
Dividing the time by 2 isn't how you find average speed. It's the total distance for the whole trip divided by the total time. So what do you get with 240 miles over those 6 hours?
wait so that makes it 40 then
Yeah, 240 miles over 6 hours lands at 40 mph. Why do you think it comes out lower than just splitting the two speeds like you first did?
idk maybe cos 4 hours is a lot more than 2
Yeah, that longer stretch at the slower speed pulls the whole average down. How would you explain in your own words what average speed actually measures over the full trip?
its just the total distance divided by the total time it took
Nice, you got the key idea right there. How come averaging the speeds like that at the start didn't match up with the total distance over total time?
cos halving it doesn't count the extra hours going slow
Exactly, the unequal times throw off just halving the speeds. How would you set this up if the trip had three speeds instead of two on the same route?
just do total distance divided by the total time for all 3
You nailed it again with total distance over total time. Looking back, how did your thinking shift once you tried calculating with an actual distance instead of just averaging the speeds?
seeing the actual hours showed me just halving it doesnt work
That breakdown with the hours really highlighted it. How might you apply the total distance over total time idea if the two legs of the trip had different distances?
u just add both distances up and divide by the total time
Right, adding up all the distances and dividing by the full time covers any case. What part of this whole process surprised you the most when you first tried the Delhi to Agra example?
prob just that it was 40 instead of 45 tbh
Yeah, that 40 instead of 45 throws a lot of people at first. How would you remind yourself next time not to just average the speeds without the times?
ill just remember to pick a distance first to check
Picking a distance first is a solid move to see the times play out. Can you walk through why that leads to 40 mph for the round trip instead of anything else?
cos 240 miles divided by 6 hours is just 40
